page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-192 is a high-capacity compute instance powered by 192 dedicated vCPUs from a 96-core Intel Xeon 8581C processor. Operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this server features a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The system is equipped with 720 GB of system memory, providing a ratio of 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores placing in the top 10% of tested systems. The Intel Xeon architecture delivers exceptional memory bandwidth, exceeding 577 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Multi-threaded operations scale efficiently, as demonstrated by top-tier results in bzip3 decompression, software compilation, and static web serving throughput. Single-core performance, however, is moderate, aligning with the middle 50% in stress-ng single-core tests.

This instance is highly suited for highly parallelized workloads such as large-scale software compilation, multi-threaded database operations, and CPU-based machine learning inference, where its AMX instructions accelerate matrix operations. The lack of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPUs represents a clear tradeoff, requiring network-attached storage for persistent data and limiting its utility for heavy graphics processing. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high physical core density and dedicated resource allocation provide strong compute-per-resource value for enterprise-scale parallel processing.
